tasks.gr12-prescribed-texts-orientation-t1: Topic: Grade 12 English HL prescribed-text orientation. Cover prescribed drama, novel and poetry study, key literary terminology, quotation support, contextual questioning and the structure of Papers 1, 2 and 3. Ask learners to identify paper demands, choose strong quotation evidence, distinguish theme from plot, interpret common literature terminology and explain how to prepare a quotation bank for NSC study.
tasks.gr12-literary-essay-contextual-skills-t1: Topic: Grade 12 English HL literary essay and contextual-response skills. Cover essay planning, thesis statements, paragraph development, contextual questions, extract-based analysis and linking details to whole-text meaning. Ask learners to choose stronger thesis statements, identify effective evidence, distinguish contextual from essay responses and improve analytical paragraphs using formal literary terminology.
tasks.gr12-paper3-essay-writing-t1: Topic: Grade 12 English HL Paper 3 essay writing. Cover narrative, descriptive, reflective, discursive and argumentative essays, planning, introductions, paragraph unity, and the full process-writing cycle. Ask learners to match prompts to essay types, choose strong thesis or reflection lines, identify features of each genre and improve structure, coherence and style in essay openings and body paragraphs.
tasks.gr12-paper1-language-practice-t1: Topic: Grade 12 English HL Paper 1 language practice. Cover comprehension strategies, summary rules, visual literacy, editing, inference, diction, tone and oral-preparation habits. Ask learners to identify main ideas, choose strong inferences, avoid summary penalties, interpret advertisements or cartoons and correct language errors in short edited passages.
tasks.gr12-oral-paper4-tasks-t1: Topic: Paper 4 Orals: The Tasks and the 50 Marks. Cover what Paper 4 is, that the orals are internally set and assessed and externally moderated, the marks (prepared speech 2 x 10, unprepared speech 15, listening for comprehension 15, total 50 of 300), what each task assesses, the oral tasks by term, and suggested durations. Ask Grade 12 learners to add marks, name the task, or place a task in its term.
tasks.gr12-listening-comprehension-t1: Topic: Listening for Comprehension. Cover the three phases of the listening process, the kinds of listening, listening critically (fact and opinion, emotive language, bias, tone), making notes, and the Grade 12 audio clip of about three minutes. Ask Grade 12 learners to name a phase or kind of listening, tell a fact from an opinion, or choose the best note-making method.
tasks.gr12-prepared-unprepared-speeches-t1: Topic: Prepared and Unprepared Speeches. Cover audience and purpose, organisational patterns, introduction and conclusion, types of proof, verbal and non-verbal delivery, and the unprepared speech with its suggested durations. Ask Grade 12 learners to name a pattern or technique, judge a piece of evidence, or plan a short speech.
tasks.gr12-p1-vocabulary-figures-t1: Topic: Paper 1 vocabulary and figures of speech (Grade 12 English HL, Term 1). Cover synonyms, antonyms, homophones, homonyms, one word for a phrase, figures of speech (simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole, oxymoron, paradox, irony, sarcasm, euphemism, onomatopoeia, synecdoche), idioms, proverbs, word origins and prefixes, roots and suffixes. Ask the learner directly (you), never about learners or CAPS. Use original short sentences, never a published text.
tasks.gr12-p1-summary-writing-t1: Topic: Paper 1 summary writing (Grade 12 English HL, Term 1). Cover the 10-mark summary of a passage of about 350 words in 80 to 90 words, selecting seven points, leaving out examples and opinion, writing in your own words and counting words (a hyphenated word and a contraction count as one). Give all texts and counts in the question. Ask the learner directly (you), never about learners or CAPS. Use original short sentences, never a published text.
